ios:
VERIFIED (Apple docs fetched 2026-10-07):
- BGTaskScheduler (iOS 13+) is the only way to be launched in the background by a timer-ish mechanism, and it is NOT time-exact. Apple's "Choosing Background Strategies": "The system decides the best time to launch your background task, and provides your app up to 30 seconds of background runtime" (BGAppRefreshTask). BGProcessingTask "can take minutes" and is meant for idle/charging periods (requiresExternalPower / requiresNetworkConnectivity). earliestBeginDate is a floor only. Apple DTS (forum thread 725675, Feb 2023): app-refresh timing is "primarily driven by device condition and user activity"; rarely-used apps may get no refresh at all. Submitting the same identifier replaces the previous request (one pending per id). Adding BGTaskSchedulerPermittedIdentifiers to Info.plist disables the legacy performFetchWithCompletionHandler API. Required: Signing & Capabilities > Background Modes > "Background fetch" (UIBackgroundModes: fetch) for refresh, "Background processing" (UIBackgroundModes: processing) for processing; Info.plist array BGTaskSchedulerPermittedIdentifiers with each task id; register all handlers before app launch finishes (AppDelegate didFinishLaunching). Expiration handler + setTaskCompleted required or the system terminates the app.
- Not covered: if the user force-quits from the app switcher, iOS stops launching the app for background tasks until the user opens it again (workmanager docs state this; Apple's BGContinuedProcessingTask page confirms "The system cancels any running tasks if a person closes the app in the app switcher"). Background App Refresh off or Low Power Mode also suppresses BG tasks (community-verified; check UIApplication.shared.backgroundRefreshStatus).
- iOS 26 BGContinuedProcessingTask (Apple "Performing long-running tasks on iOS and iPadOS"): starts in the FOREGROUND in response to a user action, shows progress in a system Live Activity, can use network/CPU after the user backgrounds the app. Useful to finish an upload the user just started ("Post now" with large media), NOT for a future-dated post.
- Background URLSession: URLSessionTask.earliestBeginDate (iOS 11+) only guarantees the load "will not begin sooner"; "does not guarantee that the load will begin at the specified date" and "has no effect for tasks created from nonbackground sessions". It cannot be used as an exact scheduler, and the request must be fully formed in advance (the platform API call with the user's token and media). It works for "finish this upload after the user backgrounds the app", not "post at 9:00 tomorrow".
- Local notifications (UserNotifications): "The system handles delivery... If the delivery occurs when your app isn't running or in the background, the system interacts with the user for you." No app code runs at delivery; your code runs only when the user taps the notification or one of its actions (userNotificationCenter(_:didReceive:)), at which point "the system launches your app in the background" (for action buttons) or foreground (default tap). UNNotificationServiceExtension runs ONLY for remote (push) notifications with mutable-content:1, never for local ones, so it is not a loophole. iOS keeps only the 64 most recently scheduled pending local notifications (flutter_local_notifications docs).
- Silent/background push (content-available:1, apns-priority 5) wakes the app with up to 30 s of runtime, rate-limited at >3/hour, and REQUIRES A SERVER (APNs provider) - out of scope for a local-first app, note it as the only "wake at a time" primitive Apple offers.
- What Buffer/Later do ("notification publishing"/"reminders", Buffer & Later help centers, 2025): their server sends a push at the scheduled time; the user taps it; the mobile app downloads media to the camera roll, copies the caption to the clipboard, and opens Instagram where the user finishes posting. Buffer: "There is no way to complete a notification post from your desktop"; it requires the mobile app installed, device linked, push enabled, otherwise "the post will not be published". For Crier the same UX is achievable with a LOCAL notification instead of a push (no server): schedule UNCalendarNotificationTrigger at the post time; on tap, the app launches and publishes via API immediately (or hands off to the share route). Local notifications fire at the exact time regardless of app state (unless the user force-quit AND the device is... no: local notifications still fire after force-quit; only BG tasks stop).
- Flutter packages: workmanager 0.10.10 (fluttercommunity, verified publisher, published ~Sep 2026) wraps BGTaskScheduler; its docs: "initialDelay is a floor, not a time", "Each link runs whenever iOS chooses, so intervals drift and can stretch to hours", registerProcessingTask is iOS-only, registerPeriodicTask minimum 15 min on Android. flutter_local_notifications 22.3.1 (dexterx.dev, verified; 23.0.0-dev prerelease) supports zonedSchedule on iOS/macOS and runs Dart only on tap (onDidReceiveNotificationResponse), not at fire time. flutter_background_service 5.1.0 is ~21 months stale and on iOS just wraps BGAppRefresh/BGProcessing (15-30 s bursts, not continuous).
Live Activities: irrelevant (display-only, no code execution at a time).
UNVERIFIED (recollection, could not fetch a page): BGProcessingTask can get several minutes (commonly cited "a few minutes to tens of minutes"); the "within next two days if used in the past week" heuristic comes from WWDC 2019/2020 talks; beginBackgroundTask grants roughly 30 s since iOS 13 (previously ~3 min).
android:
VERIFIED (developer.android.com and Play policy pages fetched 2026-10-07):
- WorkManager: PeriodicWorkRequest minimum interval 15 min (flex min 5 min); OneTimeWorkRequest.setInitialDelay exists but "WorkManager work is not guaranteed to run at exact times"; Doze defers JobScheduler-backed work to maintenance windows; App Standby buckets throttle it. Good for "retry publishing until it succeeds", bad for "post at 09:00:00".
- AlarmManager exact alarms: setExact / setExactAndAllowWhileIdle / setAlarmClock require SCHEDULE_EXACT_ALARM (Android 12+, user-revocable, "Alarms & reminders" special access) or USE_EXACT_ALARM (Android 13+, normal permission, auto-granted, not revocable). Android 14 change: SCHEDULE_EXACT_ALARM is DENIED BY DEFAULT for newly installed apps targeting API 33+ that are not calendar/alarm-clock apps (kept if already granted before upgrade; also denied after backup-restore). Calling the exact APIs without it throws SecurityException. Check AlarmManager.canScheduleExactAlarms(), send the user to Settings.ACTION_REQUEST_SCHEDULE_EXACT_ALARM, and listen for AlarmManager.ACTION_SCHEDULE_EXACT_ALARM_PERMISSION_STATE_CHANGED to reschedule. Exemption: apps on the power allowlist (ACTION_REQUEST_IGNORE_BATTERY_OPTIMIZATIONS) may use exact alarms without the permission.
- Google Play policy on USE_EXACT_ALARM (support.google.com/googleplay/android-developer/answer/13161072): only "an alarm or timer app" or "a calendar app that shows event notifications" may declare it; everyone else: "evaluate if using SCHEDULE_EXACT_ALARM as an alternative is an option". Enforcement date from community sources: after 31 July 2023 (UNVERIFIED exact date; the policy page I fetched has no date). A cross-posting app is NOT eligible: use SCHEDULE_EXACT_ALARM and ask the user. REQUEST_IGNORE_BATTERY_OPTIMIZATIONS: Play prohibits it "unless the core function of the app is adversely affected"; the official acceptable-use table lists "Task automation app - core function is scheduling automated actions" as Acceptable, which is arguably Crier's case, but treat as a last-resort opt-in toggle, not a default.
- Doze: setAndAllowWhileIdle/setExactAndAllowWhileIdle fire in Doze but "cannot fire alarms more than once per nine minutes, per app"; setAlarmClock "continues to fire normally; the system exits Doze shortly before these alarms fire" and shows the alarm icon in the status bar. Doze also suspends network access except during maintenance windows, so an alarm receiver that needs network should start a foreground service or use a wake lock + rely on the allow-while-idle window.
- Starting a foreground service from the background (Android 12+ restriction) is explicitly exempted when "App invokes an exact alarm to complete an action that the user requests" - so alarm receiver -> startForegroundService(dataSync) is allowed. Android 14+: service type must be declared (android:foregroundServiceType="dataSync", permission FOREGROUND_SERVICE + FOREGROUND_SERVICE_DATA_SYNC) and apps targeting 34+ must declare FGS types in Play Console with a description and a video link; Play wants dataSync for "user-initiated features" (a user-scheduled post qualifies). Android 15: dataSync FGS limited to 6 h per 24 h and cannot be started from BOOT_COMPLETED. Alternative: shortService type (~3 min, no extra permission) is enough for a few API calls.
- Process death: swiping the app from Recents does not cancel alarms; "Force stop" cancels all alarms and blocks receivers until the user opens the app again; always re-register alarms on BOOT_COMPLETED and on app start. OEM killers (Xiaomi/Huawei/Realme etc.) additionally need autostart/no-battery-restriction toggles (community sources, dontkillmyapp).
- Flutter packages: android_alarm_manager_plus 5.1.2 (fluttercommunity verified publisher, published ~1 Oct 2026, actively maintained: 5.0.0 raised AGP>=8.12.1/Gradle>=8.13/Kotlin 2.2). API: AndroidAlarmManager.oneShotAt(DateTime, id, callback, exact:true, wakeup:true, allowWhileIdle:true, alarmClock:bool, rescheduleOnReboot:true). Callback runs in a separate background isolate (needs @pragma('vm:entry-point'), no shared memory, must re-init plugins/DB). The plugin does NOT request SCHEDULE_EXACT_ALARM for you: on Android 14 you must check/request it (permission_handler Permission.scheduleExactAlarm, or flutter_local_notifications' requestExactAlarmsPermission()). workmanager 0.10.10 (fluttercommunity, Sep 2026) wraps WorkManager: registerOneOffTask(initialDelay, constraints, existingWorkPolicy, backoffPolicy, inputData), periodic min 15 min; use it for retries, not for the exact trigger. flutter_local_notifications 22.3.1: zonedSchedule(androidScheduleMode: AndroidScheduleMode.exactAllowWhileIdle | alarmClock | inexact), requestExactAlarmsPermission(); scheduled notifications are delivered by the OS but Dart runs only when tapped.
UNVERIFIED: fully-qualified receiver/service class names in the android_alarm_manager_plus manifest (dev.fluttercommunity.plus.androidalarmmanager.*) are from memory of the README; copy them from the package README.
windows:
VERIFIED:
- No OS-level "run my Dart code at time T" for an unpackaged Flutter desktop app; the practical design is: keep the app process alive (start at login + hide to tray) and run an in-process timer that wakes every N seconds and publishes due posts. Store due posts durably (SQLite) and on every launch publish anything overdue ("catch-up"), because the machine may have been off.
- launch_at_startup 0.5.1 (leanflutter.dev, verified publisher; last published ~18 months ago, stable but low activity): writes HKCU\Software\Microsoft\Windows\CurrentVersion\Run; MSIX-packaged apps use packageName (StartupTask). Setup: launchAtStartup.setup(appName:, appPath: Platform.resolvedExecutable, packageName: optional); enable()/disable()/isEnabled(). Users can still disable the entry in Settings > Apps > Startup; show the real state from isEnabled().
- tray_manager 0.7.0 (leanflutter.dev, published ~Sep 2026; 0.6+ rebuilt on nativeapi, legacy 0.5 API via package:tray_manager/legacy.dart) for the tray icon and context menu; window_manager 0.5.2 (leanflutter.dev, ~3 months old; migrating to nativeapi) for the minimize-to-tray behaviour: setPreventClose(true), onWindowClose -> hide() (+ setSkipTaskbar(true)), show() from the tray menu.
- Task Scheduler alternative: Register-ScheduledTask with New-ScheduledTaskTrigger -Once -At <time>, New-ScheduledTaskAction -Execute <crier.exe> -Argument "--publish <postId>", and New-ScheduledTaskSettingsSet -WakeToRun -AllowStartIfOnBatteries -StartWhenAvailable (StartWhenAvailable runs it late if the machine was off). WakeToRun = "Task Scheduler wakes the computer before it runs the task" (also the GUI checkbox "Wake the computer to run this task"; XML <WakeToRun>true</WakeToRun>). This is the ONLY way to wake the PC. Caveats (community, MS Q&A): it needs "Allow wake timers" enabled in the power plan, S3 sleep only - Modern Standby laptops generally do not wake from Task Scheduler, and it never powers on a shut-down PC. Creating a task does not need admin for the current user; it spawns a second process, so the app needs a single-instance/IPC story (or run a `crier --publish` CLI mode that exits). Judgement: offer as an opt-in "power user" option; default is tray + timer + catch-up.
- Toast notifications: flutter_local_notifications 22.3.1 has a Windows implementation (C++/WinRT toasts; needs Flutter >=3.38.1). zonedSchedule works for a one-shot (OS-delivered scheduled toast; "will only set a notification on the scheduledDate and not repeat"); periodicallyShow throws UnsupportedError; cancel() and getActiveNotifications() only work with package identity (MSIX), otherwise cancel does nothing. Alternatives: local_notifier 0.1.6 (leanflutter, ~2 years old, immediate-only, WinToast) and windows_notification 1.3.0 (mrtnetwork, ~2 years old, custom toast XML, immediate-only). Use toasts for "Posted to X" / "Post failed, tap to retry", with the app's own timer doing the actual work.
UNVERIFIED: an unpackaged app needs a Start Menu shortcut with an AppUserModelID for toasts to appear reliably (WinToast behaviour); Windows Task Scheduler minimum trigger granularity is 1 minute.
macos:
VERIFIED:
- Same model as Windows: resident process (menu-bar/tray item) + in-process timer + catch-up on launch. macOS never launches an app at a future time for you unless you register a LaunchAgent with StartCalendarInterval (launchd) - possible but a second process.
- Login item: SMAppService (macOS 13+): SMAppService.mainApp.register()/unregister(), status (.enabled, .requiresApproval, .notRegistered, .notFound), SMAppService.openSystemSettingsLoginItems(); the user sees it under System Settings > General > Login Items and may need to approve it. SMAppService.agent(plistName:) registers a LaunchAgent whose plist lives in the bundle at Contents/Library/LaunchAgents/<plist> (Label + BundleProgram Contents/MacOS/<helper>), useful only if you want a separate headless helper. launch_at_startup 0.5.1 on macOS uses sindresorhus/LaunchAtLogin (legacy helper-bundle approach, added via SwiftPM in Xcode, macOS 10.13+); the author's LaunchAtLogin-Modern (macOS 13+) is the SMAppService-based successor and notes the Mac App Store requires launch-at-login to be enabled "in response to a user action". Recommendation: write a 20-line Swift MethodChannel calling SMAppService.mainApp directly instead of depending on the legacy helper.
- Menu bar app: set LSUIElement = true in macos/Runner/Info.plist ("agent app that runs in the background and doesn't appear in the Dock") or toggle NSApp.setActivationPolicy(.accessory) at runtime; tray_manager 0.7.0 provides the status item (isIconTemplate for dark/light menu bar); window_manager setPreventClose + hide; in AppDelegate.swift return false from applicationShouldTerminateAfterLastWindowClosed.
- App Nap (Apple Energy Efficiency Guide): an app becomes a candidate when it isn't foreground, hasn't recently drawn, isn't audible, holds no IOKit/NSProcessInfo assertions, isn't using OpenGL; effects are priority reduction, TIMER THROTTLING and I/O throttling. A hidden tray app with a Dart Timer WILL have its timers coalesced/delayed. Fix: around the publishing window call ProcessInfo.processInfo.beginActivity(options: [.userInitiatedAllowingIdleSystemSleep] or .background, reason: "Scheduled post") and endActivity(_:) afterwards (macOS 10.9+). Flutter wrapper: macos_process_activity 0.2.0 (unverified single author, ~2 months old; run()/start()/end(), default .userInitiated). Do not hold .idleSystemSleepDisabled permanently; take it only a few minutes before a post is due if you want to stop the Mac from sleeping, and be explicit in the UI. A sleeping Mac will not run your timer; schedule a `pmset schedule wake` requires sudo - not viable; rely on catch-up when it wakes.
- Notifications: flutter_local_notifications supports macOS via UNUserNotificationCenter: set UNUserNotificationCenter.current().delegate in AppDelegate (the plugin docs require it), call requestPermissions(alert:, badge:, sound:), zonedSchedule for OS-delivered reminders; Dart runs only on click. Sandboxed Mac App Store builds need com.apple.security.network.client in DebugProfile/Release .entitlements for outbound HTTP (the default Flutter macOS template ships without it).
UNVERIFIED: launchd StartCalendarInterval runs missed jobs once on wake (it does for jobs missed during sleep, not during shutdown); Dart Timer in Flutter macOS is driven by CFRunLoop timers and therefore subject to App Nap coalescing (behaviour widely reported, not tested here).
recommendation:
Architecture: one cross-platform "ScheduleEngine" over a durable queue (SQLite/drift row per scheduled post: dueAt UTC, targets, payload, status, attempts, lastError) with three layers: (1) Exact trigger - platform-specific best effort; (2) Catch-up - on every app launch/resume/network-regained, publish anything whose dueAt has passed (with a configurable "late window", e.g. skip if >24 h late unless user says "post anyway"); (3) Reminder fallback - an OS local notification at dueAt that says "Tap to publish 'Title' to X, Y" so the user can rescue the post if the trigger did not run. Never promise exactness in the UI; show "~9:00" and a per-post status chip (Scheduled / Publishing / Posted 09:00:12 / Needs your tap / Failed, retry).
Per OS: iOS - reminder-first ("notification publishing", exactly what Buffer/Later do but with a local notification instead of a server push): zonedSchedule(UNCalendarNotificationTrigger) at dueAt; on tap, open the app and publish immediately (API) or hand off to the share sheet. Additionally submit a BGAppRefreshTask (workmanager registerOneOffTask with initialDelay = dueAt - now) as an opportunistic early trigger; if it fires and succeeds, cancel the reminder. Document that force-quit disables BG tasks and that only the 64 most recent pending notifications survive. For "post now" with big media, iOS 26 BGContinuedProcessingTask (or plain beginBackgroundTask + background URLSession) lets the upload finish after the user leaves. Android - android_alarm_manager_plus oneShotAt(exact:true, wakeup:true, allowWhileIdle:true, rescheduleOnReboot:true), gated on canScheduleExactAlarms(); if denied, degrade to inexact (setWindow via exact:false) plus the reminder notification, and show a settings deep link (ACTION_REQUEST_SCHEDULE_EXACT_ALARM). In the alarm isolate start a shortService/dataSync foreground service ("Publishing to X...") to get network during Doze, then WorkManager (workmanager registerOneOffTask with NetworkType.connected + exponential backoff) for retries. Do NOT declare USE_EXACT_ALARM (Play will reject). Offer, off by default, "Ignore battery optimizations" with the Play-sanctioned "task automation" justification text. Windows/macOS - resident tray/menu-bar app: launch_at_startup (or SMAppService.mainApp on macOS), window_manager setPreventClose+hide, tray_manager icon with "Next post in 42 min" tooltip, an in-process Timer.periodic(30 s) that checks the queue, plus toast/UNUserNotificationCenter result notifications; on macOS wrap the publishing window in ProcessInfo.beginActivity to defeat App Nap. Optional power-user "Wake PC to post" on Windows via Register-ScheduledTask -WakeToRun that runs `crier.exe --publish <id>` (warn about Modern Standby). Hide platform complexity behind a single Dart interface: abstract class ExactTrigger { Future<TriggerResult> arm(ScheduledPost p); Future<void> disarm(id); Future<TriggerCapability> capability(); } with implementations AlarmTrigger (Android), ReminderTrigger (iOS), ResidentTimerTrigger (desktop).
GUI (the user asked for it to look really good): make the scheduler screen the showpiece. Use a calendar/agenda hybrid: a horizontally scrolling week strip with per-day dots coloured by network, a vertical timeline for the selected day with post cards (avatar row of target networks, thumbnail, first line, countdown), and a bottom sheet composer with a date/time picker that shows local time + the user's "audience" time zone. Make the reliability model visible and honest: a capability banner per platform ("Exact timing on", "Needs 'Alarms & reminders' permission - Fix", "iOS: you'll get a reminder at 09:00, tap to publish") with one-tap fix actions, and a status chip per post with animated state transitions (Scheduled -> Publishing (progress ring) -> Posted (checkmark) / Needs tap (pulsing) / Failed (retry)). On desktop, show the same data compactly in the tray/menu-bar menu ("Next: 'Launch thread' to Bluesky, Mastodon in 42 min", "Pause scheduling"). Use Material 3 with a dynamic colour seed, large rounded cards, subtle elevation, skeleton loaders, haptics on arm/disarm, and respect platform idioms (Cupertino date picker on iOS, native menus on macOS via tray_manager). Dark mode and reduced-motion variants from day one.

manifest_snippets.snippet:
<key>UIBackgroundModes</key>
<array>
  <string>fetch</string>
  <string>processing</string>
</array>
<key>BGTaskSchedulerPermittedIdentifiers</key>
<array>
  <string>com.crier.app.publish.refresh</string>
  <string>com.crier.app.publish.processing</string>
  <!-- if using workmanager, add its identifier(s) as documented by the plugin -->
</array>
<!-- Note: adding BGTaskSchedulerPermittedIdentifiers disables application(_:performFetchWithCompletionHandler:) -->

<manifest xmlns:android="http://schemas.android.com/apk/res/android">
  <uses-permission android:name="android.permission.INTERNET"/>
  <uses-permission android:name="android.permission.RECEIVE_BOOT_COMPLETED"/>
  <uses-permission android:name="android.permission.WAKE_LOCK"/>
  <!-- Exact alarms: user-grantable, denied by default on Android 14 for non-calendar/alarm apps -->
  <uses-permission android:name="android.permission.SCHEDULE_EXACT_ALARM"/>
  <!-- Do NOT add USE_EXACT_ALARM: Google Play only allows it for alarm/timer/calendar apps -->
  <uses-permission android:name="android.permission.POST_NOTIFICATIONS"/>
  <uses-permission android:name="android.permission.FOREGROUND_SERVICE"/>
  <uses-permission android:name="android.permission.FOREGROUND_SERVICE_DATA_SYNC"/>
  <!-- optional, opt-in only; Play policy: justify as task-automation app -->
  <!-- <uses-permission android:name="android.permission.REQUEST_IGNORE_BATTERY_OPTIMIZATIONS"/> -->

  <application ...>
    <!-- android_alarm_manager_plus (copy exact class names from the package README) -->
    <service
        android:name="dev.fluttercommunity.plus.androidalarmmanager.AlarmService"
        android:permission="android.permission.BIND_JOB_SERVICE"
        android:exported="false"/>
    <receiver
        android:name="dev.fluttercommunity.plus.androidalarmmanager.AlarmBroadcastReceiver"
        android:exported="false"/>
    <receiver
        android:name="dev.fluttercommunity.plus.androidalarmmanager.RebootBroadcastReceiver"
        android:enabled="false"
        android:exported="false">
      <intent-filter>
        <action android:name="android.intent.action.BOOT_COMPLETED"/>
      </intent-filter>
    </receiver>

    <!-- flutter_local_notifications scheduled notifications -->
    <receiver android:name="com.dexterous.flutterlocalnotifications.ScheduledNotificationReceiver" android:exported="false"/>
    <receiver android:name="com.dexterous.flutterlocalnotifications.ScheduledNotificationBootReceiver" android:exported="false">
      <intent-filter>
        <action android:name="android.intent.action.BOOT_COMPLETED"/>
        <action android:name="android.intent.action.MY_PACKAGE_REPLACED"/>
        <action android:name="android.intent.action.QUICKBOOT_POWERON"/>
        <action android:name="com.htc.intent.action.QUICKBOOT_POWERON"/>
      </intent-filter>
    </receiver>

    <!-- Your own publishing foreground service (Android 14+ requires the type) -->
    <service
        android:name=".PublishForegroundService"
        android:foregroundServiceType="dataSync"
        android:exported="false"/>
  </application>
</manifest>

<key>LSUIElement</key>
<true/>  <!-- menu-bar only app: no Dock icon. Omit if you want a normal Dock app that can also hide to the menu bar. -->

<key>com.apple.security.app-sandbox</key>
<true/>
<key>com.apple.security.network.client</key>
<true/>  <!-- required for outbound HTTP in a sandboxed build; Flutter template omits it -->

$action  = New-ScheduledTaskAction -Execute "C:\\Program Files\\Crier\\crier.exe" -Argument "--publish 42"
$trigger = New-ScheduledTaskTrigger -Once -At "2026-10-08T09:00:00"
$settings = New-ScheduledTaskSettingsSet -WakeToRun -AllowStartIfOnBatteries -DontStopIfGoingOnBatteries -StartWhenAvailable
Register-ScheduledTask -TaskName "Crier\\Publish-42" -Action $action -Trigger $trigger -Settings $settings -Force
# WakeToRun needs 'Allow wake timers' enabled in the power plan and S3 sleep; Modern Standby devices usually will not wake.
